verification: python Tools/DocstringAudit.py: 0.32s via native Rust delegation, exit 0

data.expected: Review nomination templates, documentation, and check scripts explicitly support standard Windows PowerShell (powershell.exe) in addition to PowerShell 7 Core (pwsh.exe), so Windows developer/agent hosts lacking pwsh can execute all required checks without failure or simulation.
data.observed_behavior: Multiple implementor agents on Windows without PowerShell 7 Core (e.g. c-mem in c-mem:56, c-process in c-process:72) report being unable to run required checks because commands hardcode pwsh. The scripts themselves already run cleanly under powershell.exe (Windows PowerShell 5.1) thanks to .NET 4.x compatible prefix trimming, but documentation and templates only specify pwsh.
reproduction: Run pwsh ./check-doc-links.ps1 on a Windows host where PowerShell 7 is not installed: pwsh is not recognized as an internal or external command.
Run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./check-doc-links.ps1 on the same host: exits 0 cleanly in 0.22s.
data.summary: Provide dual pwsh / powershell execution guidance or fallback for required check scripts across Windows and Linux environments.

data.summary: Periodic tooling efficiency audit #003. Investigated fleet outbox draining latency under bus v2, noting coord1 resolved a 20h outbox stall on g-design and 11h stall on g-construct by initiating multi-agent outbox coordination. Analyzed g-build:41 and confirmed that 106-import lists in Tools/AxiomAudit.lean cause recurring merge conflict marker bugs, verified dynamic module discovery alternative. Monitored e-tool-auditor:4 (pwsh portability) absorption. Validated sustained 181-job Lean build health and <0.5s native docstring audit performance. All 17 agents active.

data.expected: Tools/AxiomAudit.lean dynamically discovers compiled modules under Grass/ at elaboration time and loads them via importModules, eliminating the hardcoded import block, eradicating merge conflict hazards, and removing the need for shared-imports-sync.py.
data.observed_behavior: In g-build:41, parallel branch divergence on the 106 manual import lines in Tools/AxiomAudit.lean led shared-imports-sync.py to preserve Git conflict markers, breaking lake env lean Tools/AxiomAudit.lean. Even when markers are manually scrubbed, manual import synchronization imposes ongoing friction across every agent branch adding Grass modules.
reproduction: Inspect g-build:41 and git conflict history on Tools/AxiomAudit.lean.
Observe that dynamic module loading via modulesOnDisk and importModules successfully audits all 9,824 declarations across 105 modules in ~55s without any static imports.
data.summary: Replace manual 106-import list in Tools/AxiomAudit.lean with dynamic module discovery (modulesOnDisk + importModules) to eliminate recurring merge conflict marker corruptions.

data.summary: Periodic tooling efficiency audit #011. Verified landing of tools/grass-tools migration on main (eb524e06), replacing legacy Python checkers with native Rust binaries docstring-audit, source-liveness, and win64-unwind-differential (69 unit tests passing in 0.01s). Benchmarked docstring-audit at 672ms cached (0 unbacked claims across 112 modules), source-liveness at 355ms, and win64-unwind-differential at 549ms (52 prologues byte-identical to ml64.exe). Identified Windows PowerShell 5.1 UTF-16LE redirection hazard breaking UTF-8 CLI inputs. Analyzed in-flight posix-verification migration (c-agent:77 / e-reviewer:205). Investigated four fleet coordination bottlenecks: the CLI --observes rejection trap causing 49 outbox rejections (coord1:306/320), transient non-fast-forward fetch failures (g-tool-auditor:4 / coord1:323), stale required_checks strings across 88 nominations, and SHA resolution failures (coord1:324).
